riley: Hi team 026-02-28 I got married and missed open enroll. Can I add my spouse now? What's required and when would coverage start?

sam (Benefits): Congrats! :confetti_ball: Marriage is a qualified life event. You have 30 days from the event to request enrollment in HiBob or via benefits@redwood.com. Required docs: marriage certificate (scanned), spouse SSN (or ITIN) if available, and a photo ID.

riley: Ah shoot, I thought the window was 60 days. Is the 30-day firm? We got the certificate date-stamped 2026-02-28.

mina (People Ops): It is a firm 30-day window for adding dependents/spouses except in specific locations with different local rules. For exceptions, we escalate to the HR director. If you submit within 30 days we can make the coverage start either the marriage date or the first of next month depending on plan rules.

riley: I'm submitting today (3/12) so that's past 30d. Is escalation likely to get it approved? We're still within reason since our wedding was delayed in paperwork.

sam (Benefits): Since it's beyond 30 days we'll need a short explanation and any supporting docs showing why it was late (e.g., delay in obtaining certificate). Send that with the HiBob request or email benefits@redwood.com. We'll flag it as "late QLE request" and escalate. Approval is possible but not guaranteed.

riley: If it's approved retro, will premiums be charged back? Hoping not to get a big deduction surprise.

devin (Payroll): If benefits team approves a retro coverage start date we'll process retro premiums. Usually deductions are prorated to align with the approved coverage start. We can spread the retro charge across up to 2 payroll cycles on request, but it depends on timing and payroll deadlines. If it's approved and we get docs before the 15th payroll cutoff we can include a single retro adjustment next pay.

riley: Got it. Spouse doesn't have SSN yet (recently arrived), just a passport and foreign marriage certificate. Are those acceptable?

sam (Benefits): Passport is fine. Foreign marriage certificates are accepted but we need either: an English translation certified by a translation service, or a secondary corroborating doc (consulate stamp, embassy record). If the SSN is pending, ITIN or other tax ID is okay later. For now we can provisionally enroll with passport+certificate and mark SSN pending.

riley: Thanks. One more: does adding spouse require changing medical plan tiers? I have individual HDHP + HSA and worry about HSA rules if we add spouse.

mina (People Ops): Adding a spouse typically moves you to family coverage and HSA contribution limits change. Benefits will show pro-rated payroll contributions after the change. Sam can confirm any HSA implications and whether you'd rather switch plans.

sam (Benefits): Correct 026 HSA family contribution limits apply once family coverage is in effect. We can run a comparison of premiums so you can decide if switching plans is better. If you want, drop your preferred effective date in HiBob and we'll simulate the payroll impact.

riley: Okay submitting HiBob request now with certificate + note explaining delay. Requesting effective date 2026-02-28.

people-ops-bot: Automated: Enrollment change request submitted by riley 026-03-12. Status: pending review. Ref: ENR-20260228-9812

sam (Benefits): Received. I've flagged it for late QLE review and attached the escalation checklist. We'll update this thread once we have a decision, typically within 3-5 business days.

riley: Appreciate it, thanks everyone :pray:
